band_fit.note: Published 410 cal (within 400-650) and 28g carbs (<=35g) both clear the band; no seafood; scalable to 14 by weigh-and-divide. Ruled on published numbers as instructed. Sits at the low-cal edge (410) with the baguette croutons as the sole carb load, but published figures clear the gate.

dupe_check.vs_catalog: NOT a duplicate. Nearest catalog match is 'slow-cooker-french-onion-chicken-bowls' (chicken-breast + condensed-french-onion-soup + rice + swiss-cheese). Shares protein (chicken) and flavor family (French onion) but differs on starch (rice bowl vs baguette-crouton crust) and method (slow-cooker bowl served over rice vs oven-baked, cheese-gratineed casserole) - only 2 of 4 axes match, and the plates are genuinely different (a soupy rice bowl vs a gratineed bistro bake). 'smothered-chicken-onion-gravy' and 'french-chicken-fricassee' (accepted) are unrelated (pan-smothered / white braise).
dupe_check.vs_accepted_slugs: No collision; read fresh, no french-onion chicken bake present.

cross_protein_flags: Structurally a French-onion + caramelized-onion + Gruyere/bread-gratin BAKE. Catalog already has a BEEF French-onion (french-onion-pot-roast-bowls, a rice bowl) and the candidate's own note cites a PORK french-onion-chops dish - a beef or pork 'French onion <protein> casserole/gratin' in another selector's pool would be the same plate with a swapped protein; decider should watch for a beef/pork/turkey French-onion baked-gratin twin.
evidence: French bistro oven bake: diced chicken breast + deeply caramelized onions + garlic + balsamic + broth, topped with toasted baguette and Gruyere and baked - bound by cheese, not pasta; distinct from the catalog's slow-cooker french-onion chicken RICE BOWL.
confidence: high on numbers (read from source recipe card); keep is solid on dish-identity grounds
